_readme: Floor 0 story text. PLACEHOLDER lines, replace with the real script. Keep the ids. A line may start with 'Name[expression]: '. Expressions: donnie neutral/worried/angry/shocked, dan neutral/tired/asleep/annoyed, ryker neutral/friendly/serious/shocked. Kidnappers: Yuvie, Adi, Irshad. A line with no name is Donnie thinking (his face shows; '[worried] text' sets his expression). Once someone else has spoken in an entry, use 'Donnie: ' to switch back to him.

lines: [neutral] Clocked in. The celebration over the weekend has made the place so dusty. Yesterday's cleaning wasn't enough.
Gear first. It's all in the janitor's closet, top left of the lobby.
Off to school! Don't forget to eat lunch this time. Love you, Dad.
There she is. Cart, mop, bin bags. The glamorous life.
Dan's office has had a coffee spill since Monday. Might as well start there.
Spare bin bags and a mop. I've got what I need.
The main entrance. Shift's only just started. Eight more hours.
[worried] The main entrance. I can't leave. Not without Betty.
{music:once:the_usual_suspects}I'm done. Dan's still teaching the new kid. I'll just... wring this mop out. Slowly.
Dan[tired]: Right. Let's start again.
Ryker[shocked]: Again?
Dan[annoyed]: Yes, again. Because apparently the first six times didn't take.
Ryker[friendly]: I've been taking notes!
Dan: You've drawn a dinosaur.
Ryker[serious]: That's unrelated.
Dan[tired]: Okay. One more time. This is a database. It stores information. In this case, employee records.
Ryker[friendly]: So it's like a filing cabinet.
Dan: Yes. A filing cabinet. Except it's digital, searchable, and doesn't give me a headache.
Ryker: Does it have drawers?
Dan[annoyed]: No, Ryker. It doesn't have fucking drawers.
Dan[tired]: Right. Say I want to see every employee in the company. I write: SELECT * FROM employees
Ryker[serious]: Why the star?
Dan: The star means everything. Every column. And employees is the table we're getting it from.
Ryker: Oh...
Dan[tired]: You know what? Just remember this. SELECT is what you want. Star means everything. FROM tells it where to look.
Ryker[friendly]: Got it.
Dan: Can we move on?
Ryker[serious]: So what's SQL?
Dan[annoyed]: Bro. SQL is the language we just used to talk to the database.
Ryker[friendly]: Why can't we use something normal? Like Sign Language!
Dan[annoyed]: No, Ryker. It doesn't speak Sign Language.
Dan[tired]: Anyway. What if I don't want everyone? Just certain people?
Ryker[friendly]: Then we ask nicely.
Dan[annoyed]: No. You use WHERE. SELECT * FROM employees WHERE role = 'Manager'
Ryker[shocked]: Oh! So it's like choosing who gets to be in the database?
Dan[tired]: No. They're already in the database. We're just filtering what we see. That query only shows employees whose role is Manager. Text goes in single quotes.
Ryker[serious]: Right, right. So if I put WHERE role = 'CEO'... I become the CEO?
Donnie: (Don't laugh. Don't laugh. Keep mopping.)
Not now, Raymond. I'm teaching. Allegedly.
Hi! Sorry. I'm learning databases. I think.
Dan[annoyed]: I'm going to start drinking before work.
Ryker[friendly]: Wait, I'll come too!
Dan[tired]: ...Of course you will.
Dan left his computer logged in. Still got his little cheat sheet stuck to it.
Not my business.
Unknown number. Nobody calls me during a shift.
Donnie: ...Hello?
Yuvie: Donald Raymond. Or Donnie as Betty likes to say.
Donnie[worried]: Who is this?
Yuvie: Somebody who needs you to stay very calm for the next minute.
Yuvie: Don't hang up. Don't walk anywhere. Just listen.
Yuvie: Your daughter didn't walk home from school today.
Donnie[shocked]: What?
Yuvie: Betty. Red hoodie. Brown backpack. She took the long way round. Past the old car park.
Yuvie: She's with us now.
Donnie[shocked]: No. No, no. Put her on. Put her on the phone right now.
Yuvie: She's fine. She stays fine. That part is up to you.
Donnie[angry]: If you lay one finger on her, I swear to God...
Adi: Nobody's touching her! She's eating tangy hot wings. She asked for them specifically.
Irshad: Those were mine.
Adi: She's a guest, Irshad.
Irshad: She's a hostage, Adi. You don't give the hostage my shit..
Adi: I didn't. I gave your wings.
Irshad: Yes I meant my wings not my actual... poo.
Adi: Reminds me. Lay off the peri peri. The van smells of smoke.
Yuvie: ...
Yuvie: I'm sorry about them, Donnie. Genuinely. It's been a long morning.
Yuvie: But don't mistake them for the whole operation. I'm the part you should worry about.
Yuvie: No police. No security. No 'quick word' with your supervisor. We'll know. We always know.
Donnie[worried]: ...What do you want from me?
Yuvie: Small things. To start.
Yuvie: The office you just cleaned. The computer in there is still logged in.
Irshad: There's a new face in that building. We want to know who.
Yuvie: You heard the man teaching the boy. Do what he said. Find the new one.
Donnie[worried]: I'm a janitor. I don't know anything about computers.
Yuvie: Then today's a learning day.
Donnie[worried]: Betty... Hang on, sweetheart. Okay. Okay. The computer.
Dan's computer. Still logged in. Not my business.
Ryker. The intern. Started this week.
They're calling again. Of course they are.
Yuvie: Well?
Donnie[worried]: The new one's an intern. Ryker. Started this week. Engineering, with Dan.
Irshad: An intern. Told you. Nobody important.
Yuvie: Everybody's important when they're new. Nobody knows their face yet.
Yuvie: That was good, Donnie. You follow orders. Betty will be glad to hear it.
Donnie[angry]: Let me talk to her.
Yuvie: When you've earned it.
Adi: She says hi, by the way.
Irshad: She said 'my dad is going to destroy you'.
Adi: Don't reveal that!
Irshad: Oh im sorry. uhh. she didn't say that!
Adi: He very much believes you now.
Yuvie: Both of you, out of the van.
Yuvie: Next job. Find a USB-C cable. Then go to the employee terminal on the front desk.
Donnie[worried]: A USB-C cable? Where am I supposed to find one of those?
Yuvie: You're the janitor. You know where everything in that building ends up.
Donnie[worried]: ...Right. Think, Donnie. Where would a cable be?
Is it Friday yet?
The coffee here is a war crime.
Five more minutes. Then I'll look busy.
Have you tried the new chairs? Neither have I.
Why do vending machines sell USB-C cables now?
Saw Pete buy a cable from that vending machine. Beats the crisps.
The vending machine has cables now. And still no decent sandwich.
Crisps, energy drinks and... phone cables? Nothing I need right now.
Crisps, energy drinks and... USB-C cables. Of course.
Coins only. I might have some in my locker, in the janitor's closet.
Coin in hand first. (Number keys pick what I'm holding.)
One USB-C cable. The most expensive thing I've bought from a vending machine.
I've got my cable. The rest is snacks I can't afford.
My locker. Spare socks and a sandwich of unknown age.
Spare socks, the sandwich... and a coin. Perfect.
Irshad: Got the cable?
Donnie: ...Yes.
Irshad: From the vending machine. We saw. Very dignified.
Donnie[angry]: You're watching me?
Yuvie: We're always watching you, Donnie. Keeps everyone honest.
Yuvie: We've sent you an app. KODEX. It's in your messages. Install it.
Yuvie: Plug your phone into the employee terminal. KODEX does the hard part. You learn the rest.
Adi: It's got a little book on the icon. I picked the icon.
Irshad: You downloaded the icon.
Adi: I picked which one to download.
Yuvie: One more thing. The receptionist doesn't leave that desk often. Wait for her to go.
Yuvie: If she sees you, you're just a nosy janitor. If she sees you twice, you're a problem. We don't like problems.
Donnie[worried]: ...Understood.
Install this. Don't ask questions. - Y
KODEX installed. Now the terminal, once the receptionist steps away.
The employee terminal. Not for janitors.
I should check my messages first.
Cable in hand first, so I can plug in. (Number keys.)
Receptionist: Excuse me! Away from the desk.
Receptionist: Snoop around here again and I'm raising a ticket. A big one.
Front desk. How can I not help you?
If it's not a ticket, it's not my problem.
Coffee break's at the usual time. Don't touch anything.
Coffee. Back in five.
Clearance for Floor 1. The elevator should take me up now.
Hang on, Betty.
Floor 1's open. The elevator's at the top of the lobby.
Morning, Donnie.
These quarterly reports won't file themselves. Sadly.
Is the printer on this floor broken again?
Don't mop near me, I've got new shoes.
Meeting about the meeting at ten.
If anyone asks, I'm in a call.
